page: Vultr vx1-g-64c-256g-3840s is a General Purpose server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor with 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs via hyperthreading, operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided locally via a 3840 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate strong compute capabilities, with the stress-ng single-core performance and Passmark CPU score ranking in the top tier. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and vector neural network instructions (AVX512_VNNI, AVX_VNNI, AVX512_BF16), which contribute to its top-tier performance in physics simulations and extended instruction tests. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with large-block read and write speeds reaching top-tier levels of 496.98 GB/sec and 190.5 GB/sec respectively, though the overall Passmark memory score remains in the average tier.

This server is well-suited for database operations, static web serving, and medium-scale LLM inference, as evidenced by its top-tier Passmark database operations score and strong text generation speeds on 7B parameter models. However, users should note that the CPU allocation is shared, which may introduce performance variability under sustained multi-tenant workloads. The high-density local NVMe storage and balanced resource profile offer qualitative cost efficiency for data-intensive applications that do not require dedicated CPU cores.
description: Vultr vx1-g-64c-256g-3840s is a General Purpose server in the VX1 Cloud Compute family, powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor with 64 shared vCPUs and 256.0 GB of RAM. It features 3840 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI. Benchmarks show top-tier single-core CPU performance, Passmark physics, and database operations, alongside strong multi-core and memory bandwidth capabilities. The system delivers 104.09 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and achieves 64.48 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. However, the shared CPU allocation presents a potential tradeoff for workloads requiring guaranteed, sustained compute performance, and Passmark memory scores sit in the average tier. This server is highly suited for database hosting, static web serving, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
